scope: Durable retry for digital-product fulfillment via the existing platform_jobs worker, plus a reconciliation map for the broader October-10-era checkout-expiry/digital-delivery work.
whyThisAndNotMore: The original ask was to reconcile October 10 checkout-expiry/digital-delivery work with the current platform worker. Investigation found the real reconciliation question was bigger than a merge: an unmerged branch (origin/claude/alkebulan-files-migration-aty6p0, origin/work/kebu-ecosystem-ux) independently built a job-queued commerce-hardening design (platform_jobs table+RPC, multi-line checkout reservations, shop_refunds, worker handlers for digital.fulfill and order.cancel_gift_card_failed) that duplicates/conflicts with this branch's own already-live platform_jobs infrastructure (20260920040000_platform_durability.sql, 20260920050000_platform_worker_recovery.sql, lib/platform/jobs.ts, lib/platform/worker.ts, app/api/cron/platform-worker/route.ts). Presented the architecture choice to the user; they chose job-queued. This slice implements the part of that choice that is concretely applicable to the EXISTING live architecture (durable digital-fulfillment retry) and documents, rather than silently ports, the larger unresolved piece.

implemented.lib/shop/digital-downloads.ts: Split into fulfillPaidDigitalOrder (raw core — now throws on genuine failure instead of silently swallowing it, which the original code did) and fulfillPaidDigitalOrderDurable (webhook-facing: tries the core, and on failure enqueues a digital.fulfill platform job with idempotency key digital.fulfill:<orderId> instead of throwing, so the payment provider's webhook response is unaffected by a delivery hiccup).
implemented.lib/platform/worker.ts: executeJob now handles job_type 'digital.fulfill' by calling the raw fulfillPaidDigitalOrder directly (not the durable wrapper) so a real failure propagates to runPlatformWorker's existing failPlatformJob path — proper attempt-count/exponential-backoff/dead-letter via the already-live platform_jobs machinery, not a self-perpetuating re-enqueue.
implemented.app/api/webhooks/{paystack,wave,paypal,j: All 6 call sites switched from fulfillPaidDigitalOrder to fulfillPaidDigitalOrderDurable.

bugCaughtDuringImplementation: An intermediate version had fulfillPaidDigitalOrder itself catch-and-self-enqueue on failure. That would have made the worker's own retry of a digital.fulfill job silently re-enqueue a fresh job (hitting the same idempotency key, upsert+ignoreDuplicates would no-op) and the ORIGINAL job would still be marked 'succeeded' by runPlatformWorker even though delivery never completed — a silent permanent-failure-reported-as-success bug. Caught and fixed before any test run by separating the throwing core from the non-throwing wrapper and being explicit in the worker about which one it must call.
testsAdded: tests/shop/digital-downloads.test.ts (new, 6 cases): raw core success/idempotent-reuse/throws-on-insert-failure/throws-on-email-rejection; durable wrapper never-throws-on-success/enqueues-correct-idempotency-key-on-failure.

tests/platform/worker.test.ts (+3 cases): digital.fulfill success calls the raw core; a thrown failure goes through failPlatformJob (not a re-enqueue); an invalid payload is rejected before calling the core.
testsUpdated: tests/shop/webhook-paystack.test.ts and tests/shop/payment-lifecycle.integration.test.ts: mock target renamed fulfillPaidDigitalOrder -> fulfillPaidDigitalOrderDurable to match what the webhook routes actually call now; assertions unchanged otherwise.
fullSuiteResult: typecheck 0 errors; lint 0 errors/348 warnings; vitest 5,938 passed/168 skipped (+9 tests vs. the prior checkpoint, same 3 pre-existing hosted-QA-only failures, not new); build exit 0.

deliberatelyNotPortedFromTheUnmergedBran.multiLineCheckoutReservations: origin's 20260923200000_commerce_multi_line_reservations.sql alters shop_checkout_reservations (drops unique(order_id), adds variant_id) and adds reserve_multi_shop_checkout()/cancel_shop_order(). This branch's live checkout is still single-product-per-reservation (lib/shop/stock.ts: reserveShopCheckout takes one productId/quantity). There is also a SEPARATE, older (pre-dates Sep 19) cart-based multi-item order path (lib/shop/cart-order.ts, gift cards/discounts) that does NOT use the reservation/TTL system at all — it decrements stock directly at order-creation time. Porting multi-line reservations is a product/architecture decision about unifying or choosing between these two existing checkout paths, not a mechanical migration port.
deliberatelyNotPortedFromTheUnmergedBran.giftCardCancelCompensation: The unmerged branch's order.cancel_gift_card_failed job type durably retries restoring a gift card balance after cancel_shop_order() fails. cancel_shop_order() does not exist on this branch and has no current trigger: the live cart-order.ts flow only ever rolls back a gift-card redemption that failed DURING order creation (deletes the just-inserted order, no cancellation-of-an-already-committed-order concept exists yet). Porting this job type without first deciding when/how an already-fulfilled order gets cancelled would add dead code with no reachable call site.
deliberatelyNotPortedFromTheUnmergedBran.shopRefunds: No shop_refunds table or refund UI/flow exists on this branch to hang a durable-retry job off of.

recommendationIfPursuedFurther: Treat multi-line reservations + cancel_shop_order + shop_refunds + gift-card compensation as its own vertical slice with an explicit product decision first: should the cart-based order path (lib/shop/cart-order.ts) be migrated onto the TTL-reservation system, and what does 'cancelling a paid order' mean operationally (full refund trigger? dispute? admin action?) before any schema or worker-handler work starts.
